title.narrative: Activity under preparation `She decides¿: promoting women¿s participation in political decision making

description.narrative: Women in Sri Lanka are severely underrepresented in politics and women¿s participation and leadership in decision making is virtually in-existent, despite a slight positive development in the 2024 elections which saw an increase of the number of women in the Sri Lanka Parliament (from earlier 5 to now nearly 10%). This hampers the capacity of women to participate in any decision-making fora, including related to peace-building, conflict resolution and contribute to a cohesive society. In 2024, the Government of Sri Lanka adopted their first ever National Action Plan for Women, Peace and Security (NAP WPS), where increasing women¿s political participation and leadership is one of the priorities.This Action aims to support the implementation of the NAP WPS by creating the conditions to increase women¿s political participation in Sri Lanka including by promoting an enabling environment that allows, encourages and supports their involvement and influence in political decision-making. This Action aims to overcome the obstacles that hinder women's political participation, i.e. barriers such as gatekeeping practices within political parties, pervasive stigma, harassment, online and offline gender-based violence and undue criticism. It will tackle the root causes of women's low political participation including by challenging entrenched socio-cultural norms and gender-based violence and discrimination thereby transforming gender norms and enhancing political participation. Further compounding factors that exclude women from decision making positions, are financial constraints, the prevalence of intimidation tactics, and violence deeply rooted in local political culture. The focus will be on high-level political advocacy, policy and legislative reforms where needed, implementation of policies and plans, social awareness campaigns and political trainings for young male and female leaders. In addition, an intersectional approach will ensure to address the diverse and overlapping barriers faced by women from different backgrounds, including women with disabilities, thereby leaving no one behind.By empowering women and working with, and across, political parties and young leaders to be, the action can further help breaking down existing barriers, with the aim to create a more inclusive and representative political landscape in Sri Lanka. This will lead to better decision-making and a stronger, more equitable society. The anticipated impact of this Action is to significantly increase women¿s full, equal, safe and meaningful participation in political institutions. The Action is expected to address the recommendations by EU 2024 Election Observation and Expert Missions in this regard.
